history.dynasty: Gujarat Sultanate: tomb begun 1445 CE by Muhammad Shah II, completed 1451 by Qutbuddin Ahmad Shah II; complex greatly expanded by Mahmud Begada
history.period: Tomb 1445-1451 CE; Sarkhej Lake, pavilions and palaces added mid-to-late 15th century
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE -- keep-or-drop decision needed: Sarkhej Roza is an Islamic tomb/mosque/palace complex. Shaikh Ahmed Khattu Ganj Bakhsh of Anhilwad Patan (1336-1445), friend and adviser of Ahmad Shah I, retired to Sarkhej in his later life and died here in 1445. In his honour Muhammad Shah II began the tomb in 1445; his son Qutbuddin Ahmad Shah II finished it in 1451. Mahmud Begada expanded the complex, excavating the great Sarkhej Lake, building a palace on its south-west corner, and raising a mausoleum opposite Ganj Bakhsh's tomb for himself and his family -- he, his son Muzaffar Shah II, his great-grandson Mahmud Shah III and Queen Rajbai are buried there. The architecture is credited to the Persian brothers Azam and Muazzam Khan; it fuses Persian Islamic stylistic influence with indigenous Hindu and Jain features (Indo-Saracenic). Le Corbusier compared the complex's design to the Acropolis of Athens, hence the nickname 'Acropolis of Ahmedabad'. It is a Monument of National Importance. No Hindu festivals are observed; photography rules not verified -- verify locally.

town_description: Ahmedabad, on the banks of the Sabarmati, is Gujarat's largest city, founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmad Shah I. Its historic walled old city is a UNESCO World Heritage site, and it remains a major centre of textiles, commerce and education.
